E V E N   M O R E   M A I L !

February, 1991       Page  Reply

 C.W. G. Coppin.......02    04
 Brian Thompson.......07    08
 Jon Westgate.........09    11
 Chris Powell.........12    14
 G.A. Matthews........16    20
 Raymond Hoy..........24    27
 Gerhard Behr.........30    33
 Dylan Kevin Hall.....35    35
 Philip Seddon........36    38

From: C.W.G. Coppin, BOSTON

Dear Brian,

Thank you for your suggestions
about dumping screens on the
Brother HRS printer. Sorry for
the delay in replying, I have
been away for 2 weeks.

I think you have solved the
problem.  I enclose specimen
prints using the POKES
indicated.  The result seems to
me as perfect as can be got from
the HR printer and I am very
satisfied with the results.

There is one snag though, these
results were obtained as
follows:

 1) LOADed samdos dump load.
 2) POKEd in the appropriate
    POKEs.
 3) LOADed the screen required.
 4) Entered "dump" and return
    and got the result.
Then I tried to save the code as
amended on another disk by,
SAVE "HR DUMP" code 20224,512.
It came up on the directory o.k,
but when I tried to dump a
screen all I got was o.k but no
picture.  Why?  Perhaps you can
explain.

I'd like to congratulate you on
a very fine disk magazine, and
to thank you for dealing
successfully with my problem.

        Yours sincerely,
         C.W.G. Coppin.

Brian Cavers to Mr. C.W.G.Coppin

The values aren't POKEd directly
into the DUMP code but into the
system variables. Whenever DUMP
is used, it uses those values in
the system variables. Therefore
you must re-do the POKEs EVERY
time you load the DUMP code.This
can be done by entering the
POKES in a procedure, e.g...


55000 DEF PROC DUMPHR5
55010 POKE 23074,0 :REM CODES TO
55020 POKE 23075,27:REM ADJUST
55030 POKE 23076,75:REM DUMP FOR
55040 POKE 23067,65:REM AN HR5
55050 POKE 23068,7 :REM PRINTER
55060 DUMP
55070 END PROC

If you SAVE the preceding BASIC
as say, SAVE"DUMPHR5" (note NO
LINE number for auto-run)you can
then load it whenever you want
or MERGE it permanently into any
program in which you wish to use
DUMP. You will also need to load
the "dmpld" code as usual. Now,
instead of using DUMP elsewhere
in the program or even as a
direct command, substitute the
command... DUMPHR5 which will do
the POKEs followed by DUMP.

ALTERNATIVELY, of course, you
could add to your program...

55000 LOAD "dmpld" CODE
55010 POKES....  (ALL THE POKES)
55020 RUN
       ...then save the program:
SAVE "NAME" LINE 9000.

Note that if you use the latter
method you should then use DUMP
in the usual way.

Anyway, I'm glad you can now get
proper DUMPS with your printer.

                        - Brian

From: Brian Thompson, NR. RUGBY

Dear Ron and Brian,

Like many others I continue to
be astounded by the consistently
high standards you maintain in
the OUTLET magazine.

I look forward to the SAM m/code
features which you propose for
future issues. In the meantime
maybe you or someone else can
answer a question for me. I know
how to draw a straight line in
SAM machine code with JDRAW
(013CH) using the B,C, D, and E
registers also JDRAWTO(013FH)
using the B and C registers, but
please how do you draw an arc in
SAM machine code?
               - Brian Thompson

Brian Cavers to Brian Thompson



Thanks, Brian.

Stephen Wilson has offered to do
the new SAMCLASS tutorial for us
and I'm going to try to get the
first lesson in this issue or
next month at the latest.

I've also passed on your inquiry
to Stephen who is better able to
answer it than I am.

From: Jon Westgate, HAMPSHIRE.

Dear Ron and Brian,

Perhaps you remember our short
discussion at the All Formats
fair about printing the OUTCLASS
articles,especially with respect
to the assembler listings.

As you can see from the enclosed
listings, the word wrap does
work correctly in all instances.

OUTLET Issue No. 39 did have the
changes you mentioned which
resulted in the assembler code
being printed in three columns,
however, it is still very
difficult to read the code. I
have included listings from

OUTCLASS from issues 38, 39 and
40 of OUTLET so that you can see
the differences. In all cases I
used the PRINT THIS option.

I have also included a printout
from the article SPRITEHELP in
Issue 38 (Oct. 90) of OUTLET,
where the printing is apparently
done using a different routine.

I would be very grateful if you
could find a solution or,
alternatively suggest a method
of being able to print the
OUTCLASS series.

I would like to take this
opportunity of saying how much I
enjoy OUTLET, congratulations
and keep up the good work.
     Regards, Jon Westgate.

Jon Westgate From Brian Cavers

The best I have been able to do
is to include an option of 32 or
64 column printing if you select
the SET PRINTER option in OUTLET
text mode. This is not ideal but
if you scan through OUTCLASS on
screen noting any pages you feel
would be clearer in 32 columns,
you can then print some pages in
32 column and some in 64.

I have studied the code and I do
not now think it is possible to
improve on this system without a
completely new program involving
a lot of work to retain Spectrum
compatibility. I shall have to
shelve that project for some
future dream I'm afraid! - Brian

From: Chris Powell, POWYS.

Dear Ron and Brian,

Whilst cheering the inclusion in
OUTLET of Alan Hurst's cure for
the +3/printer bug, I would like
to draw your attention to the
existence of a BASIC solution to
the problem.

It was in this very magazine
that John Cleveland(DRIVECHAT36)
shared with us his discovery of
the POKE 23399, 20. All that is
required for auto run programs
such as OUTLET's "disk"is a line
in the BASIC loader containing:

  POKE 23354,62:POKE 23355,16:
  POKE 23399,20

Without having to resort to
either a BREAK or a STOP, my
STAR LC10 works perfectly with
programs such as Artist II and
Masterfile +3.

Now, as they say, "for something
completely different". Can you
tell me anything about CP/M for
the +3? What, (if any), are its
plus points compared with the
resident system? What sort of
programs can it run and is it
worth the cash?

All the best for the new year.

           Chris

To Chris Powell from Brian Gaff

Well CP/M offers access to a
huge amount of PD software. The
Locomotive implementation comes
with Mallard Basic, which is a
more standard type than ZX. It
will run most Microsoft Basic
programs too. It also has random
and serial files and a system
called Jetsam - no I don't know
what it means either - but it
basically allows one big file to
be indexed from a smaller one.

The main problems with CP/M on a
Spectrum are the small disc
space, the screen resolution and
the poor serial port. The first
of these can be cured by an
add-on second drive, the second

is partially fixed by having a
51-column screen which is a
window onto the full 80 columns
normally required. Little can be
done about the port though!

The programs that are around are
usually business-orientated
though some languages and
assemblers are available too. As
both the CPC and PCW run CP/M, a
lot of their software runs on
the Spectrum implementation.
Don't expect user-friendliness
though -this is an old operating
system!

                         - B.G.

From: G.A.Matthews, ESSEX.

As you may remember, I bought a
Sam Coupe earlier this month.
I'd only had it for 2 days when
I last wrote. I have now had a
chance to try it out - the Basic
is great -but the tape interface
is abysmal;I had great difficul-
ty getting it to load anything.

My trusty Sanyo Dataload, which
has given splendid service on my
Spectrum, did not work with Sam.
At full blast it only read the
file name then came up with
'tape loading error'.

After trying every tape recorder
that I could lay my hands on I
finally hit the jackpot.

At the back of a cupboard I had
a Harvard deck bought at Romford
Street Market and then neglected
because my Spectrum didn't like
it, but Sam did.  I checked the
Harvard out with a tape doctor
utility, according to which the
Harvard runs 9% too fast; the
Dataloader dead on.Very strange!

This is being typed on the Sam
using Tasword 2 converted with
LERM's Samtape utility.  I have
got a lot of games across to
disk as well, they seem to run
noticeably faster.

"ROMOVER", from an Outlet tape
works. All my old tapes load
using ROMOVER, and I must say
that the Sam keyboard is a lot
better to type on than my

Sinclair Spectrum 128. (The pre-
Amstrad type).

The instructions supplied by MGT
with the Sam are lousy.  I still
haven't worked out what the
utilities are on their disk.  I
can find no reference to them.
They supplied almost no info on
the system variables.  I'll have
to get the technical reference
guide and hope it's better.


My comments on problems with
computers used with TVs, via
the Scart socket i.e., jittering
of the picture, also apply to
HITACHI and some ITT sets.  They
all have similar circuits to
give a better T.V. picture.

Unfortunately,it creates a video
blanking problem with some comp-
uters -not just the Spectrum. It
applies to the ATARI ST and
AMIGA and C64. If anyone is
thinking of buying such a set it
would be as well to warn them. I
have a GRANADA T.V. with RGB
socket. I can get a good picture
from the monitor DIN socket on
my 128 spectrum via the RGB
socket but no sound!

          G.A. Matthews

To Mr. Matthews from Brian Gaff

On SAM tape loading, I agree
that it is worse than the
Speccy. The two main reasons for
this are.

1) The input has to be able to
handle loaders with an extremely
wide frequency range. This means
that any other old rubbish that
comes out of a tape deck can
easily upset the load. A good
analogy is that the wider you
open the window, the more the
muck flies in!

2) For some odd reason, the tape
input needs a higher level than
the Spectrum and some decks
just cannot do it.

Your speed anomaly is usually
only a help if you are loading
commercial games with special
loaders. As you observe, things
do run a bit faster on SAM.
Thus, any special loaders on
games will do the same, and the
code usually then fails to load
unless you speed the deck up!
This will be the case even with
ROMOVER and EMUTILITY.

The disc utilities do seem to
change from time to time! Mine
has two translators, one for
programs on tape, and the other
for Disciple and +D ones. These
alter ZX Basic to Sam Basic.
Then there is the Emulator,
which you have no doubt found.
The Patch part seems only to
work on games.

If you could explain which util-
ities you do not understand,
maybe we could help a bit more.

SCART is a so-called standard. I
can recall all the trials we had
with the DIN standard on audio
gear. I get the feeling from
reading about SCART that it was
designed with videos in mind.
These have a very rough sync
due to their mechanical short-
comings, and the fast blanking
was obviously put in to stop
wobbly pictures.

The problem is that computers
are probably very crude in the
video department, and the
signals presented can confuse
the circuitry in the TV. Answer?

Well, I would hassle the TV
supplier because if the Speccy
works on one set, it should do
so on another!

                        - B.G.





[A fulll list of the SAM system
variables, in alphabetical as
well as address order, is in
OUTLET 40.              - B.C.]

From: Raymond Hoy, BASINGSTOKE.

OUTLET 38 was a great issue;nice
clipart and a useful (+D)program
called FINDOUT. The only thing I
found wrong was you have changed
lines in the Contents program.It
makes things a bit difficult.

I have managed to alter lines in
"FINDOUT" so you only load 2
issues onto a disc instead of 3
(which you can't do owing to the
size OUTLET has become in recent
issues). All I've done is delete
the:- LET D$="" in line 2000.
The other commands in the same
line CC=your 1st disc and EE=
your 2nd disc - not the 3rd disc
as before (editor see enclosed
listings).

It's O.K up to Issue 34 but then
you've changed line 120 where we
had to alter the RANDOMIZE USR 0
to LOAD d*"FIND". I did have a
go at changing the same commands
found in line 80 but this didn't
work properly. Do you know a
solution to this please?


If readers do use this program
to SAVE two OUTLETS on one disc
[Disciple/+D only - B.C.] they
will have to erase or move some
of the add-enders so the two
issues fit within the 80 files
allotted to our disc system and
also erase system file from each
issue to save space.

Can anyone explain what DATEL
ELECTRONICS are playing at?  If
you send them `130.00, normally
within 48 hours they will send
the order (in this case the PLUS
'D' DISC DRIVE SYSTEM).  Over a
week later they sent a friend of
mine a card to fill in promising
not to do any illegal copying.
This was sent off promptly but
he is still waiting some 4 weeks
later.  This is a disgusting way
to treat a customer.  Why didn't
they print the form in their
advert and save everyone a lot
of trouble.  They have lost any
custom I was considering and
others too I expect.
              Yours sincerely,

                  RAYMOND HOY

To Ray Hoy from Brian Cavers

I think you are being a bit hard
on Datel, Ray! Firstly, the card
that has to be filled in to say
you are not going to use the
hardware for piracy is a flaming
nuisance and a delay I agree.
However,the subsequent four week
delay could be due to many, many
different circumstances, e.g.,
lost in the post going back to
Datel or the parcel lost coming
back from Datel! Even if the
order was lost WITHIN Datel's
system it's unreasonable not to
expect this sort of thing to
happen now and again.In my view,
bad service is when you write
THREE or more times without any
reply - not the first time.

However, I accept that the two
delays together must be most
annoying!I personally would give
them four to six weeks then
write again. If no reply I would
write a rather firm but polite
letter saying the order had not
been received. If still no reply
within say, three or four weeks
I would write a very firm letter
demanding immediate action or a
refund. If still no reply then a
registered letter threatening
legal action. Of course, a phone
call or two in the middle of
that lot would also have to be
taken into account as to whether
there is a genuine mistake or
whether the merchant is messing
you about! We have an article in
OUTLET soon about mail order.

Anyway, I trust your friend has
now received his Plus D?

I had a look at your changes to
line 80 in CONTENTS and they
seem alright to me.I can't think
why they wouldn't work. Has
anyone else managed to get the
FINDOUT program to work on later
issues?
                       - Brian

From: Gerhard Behr, BRIERFIELD

You asked about the Citizen 124D
printer.  I have had one for 6
weeks now, replacing my old STAR
DP 510.  It has many interesting
features:

  1) Paper loading.
It has a push tractor feed and
anybody used to a pull feed will
appreciate the amount of paper
this saves.  In addition it will
position the paper printing 1/2
inch below the top.  This can be
adjusted manually and is very
convenient for printing address
labels.  If you want to use
single sheets, you need not
remove the continuous paper, but
press the "PARK" key to move it
temporarily out of the way.

Single sheets are then dropped
into the paper guide and will
again be adjusted automatically.
There is no paper press, but the
paper is held down against the
platen by the top cover.  This
works well for ordinary use but
is not strong enough for print -
ing on some kinds of envelopes.

  2) Fonts.
There are 3 fonts which can be
selected by a key at the front
of the printer: Draft, which is
as good as many NLQs of older
printers, prints at 120 cps and
2 LQ fonts called Times, Roman
and Courier, printing 40cps.
They are good enough for making
slides for projection - probably
the most severe test for any
printer.

  3) Special Effects.
All the Epson effects like e.g.,
emphasised, condensed,subscript,
underline, proportional etc. are
there;also shadow/outline print.
Epson or IBM emulation can be
set by dipswitches.

  4) Graphics.
It works perfectly with the
Spectrum and Kempston E inter -
face set for Epson, but I am
still unable to print graphics
with the SAM Coupe.  It works
with FLASH but is so slow, one
runs out of tea before it is
finished.  Can you tell us how
to use DUMP and DUMPLD please
(with any printer)?

          Gerhard Behr.

Brian Cavers to Gerhard Behr

Yes,just boot in your MGT system
disk and select the Screen Dump
Loader option. Alternatively,
enter BASIC at any time and
enter LOAD "dumpld"CODE.The code
is now installed but remember
you will have to reload it if
you reset the computer with the
RESET button at the back or with
RANDOMIZE USR 0 or if you switch
off the machine. However,I think
using NEW should not clear it.

Once installed you use the BASIC
command DUMP to print a picture
or DUMP CHR$ to print text only.
If you get odd results like gaps
in the picture you may need to
adjust the system variables.

In such cases,it's worth reading
my reply to Julian Bonnebaigt in
Issue 37 but if you run into
difficulties, write again with
FULL details (i.e. send a print-
out or state "nothing printed",
send details of any changes. If
your printer has a special
graphics mode or whatever).

In your case there should be no
problem since you get normal
print-outs from your Spectrum
and FLASH!

A real example of an application
of DUMP is in the next but one
letter following this by Philip
Seddon.

                        - Brian

Dylan Kevin Hall,36 Paul Street,
   Blacktown, New South Wales,
         Australia, 2148
      (Phone: 02 622 7742)

I and other Australian SAM users
need an English contact to get
various items through that would
otherwise be very cost
ineffective, e.g., to get many
third party items with multiple
bank drafts is EXPENSIVE and it
would be better if I could send
one large cheque to our contact
and get them to get the indivi-
dual items from said companies.


You're a trusting sort of bloke
ain't you, Dylan?
                        - Brian

From: Philip Seddon.

As there is no Index data on Sam
versions of Outlet I decided to
alter the Auto Menu file (Outlet
34).  On the system disc that
came with the drive is a file
called "dumpld".  Transfer this
file to the disc with your Auto
Menu on, then Edit the following
lines in the Menu programme:


30 CLEAR 45099:LOAD "dumpld"
CODE:(leave the rest of the line
alone)


430 CLS: CSIZE 8,8: PRINT
PAPER 7:PEN 0;(leave rest of
line).

Edit the last part of line 470
to read; PAPER 7;PEN 0;type$;
PAPER 0,520 LET valid$=
"ZUDLECRPHVSNMTQG" 560 CSIZE
8,8:PRINT #1;PAPER 2; AT 1,0; "
Z=Dump screen"; TAB 30;size$;
TAB 0; AT 0,0; menu$(q); TAB 0

There are 10 spaces before the Z
in line 560. Enter the following
new line 215 IF opt$="Z" THEN
DUMP.  ReSAVE with SAVE
"AUTOMENU" LINE 30

This modification works a treat
on my Star LC10 printer. Also,If
you want to print out just one
line from a program type LLIST N
TO N. The printer then just
prints line N where N is your
line number.    - Philip Seddon

Brian Cavers to Philip Seddon


Thanks, Philip.

You'll be pleased to hear that I
have now converted OUTDEX to run
on the SAM. It needs some more
preparation but should appear in
OUTLET within a few months so
you will have a proper index.


Spectrum users, envious of the
SAM's ability to LIST or LLIST
FROM... TO,can look forward to a
Spectrum program in OUTLET next
month to do the same.
                       - Brian.

To Mr. Matthews from Brian Gaff

On SAM tape loading, I agree that it is worse than the Speccy. The two main reasons for this are.

1) The input has to be able to handle loaders with an extremely wide frequency range. This means that any other old rubbish that comes out of a tape deck can easily upset the load. A good analogy is that the wider you open the window, the more the muck flies in!

2) For some odd reason, the tape input needs a higher level than the Spectrum and some decks just cannot do it.

Your speed anomaly is usually only a help if you are loading commercial games with special loaders. As you observe, things do run a bit faster on SAM. Thus, any special loaders on games will do the same, and the code usually then fails to load unless you speed the deck up! This will be the case even with ROMOVER and EMUTILITY.

From: Gerhard Behr, BRIERFIELD

You asked about the Citizen 124D printer.  I have had one for 6 weeks now, replacing my old STAR DP 510.  It has many interesting features:

**Brian Cavers для Mr. C.W.G. Coppin**

Значения не вносятся напрямую в код DUMP, а записываются в системные переменные. Всякий раз, когда используется DUMP, он берет значения именно из системных переменных. Поэтому ты должен повторно вводить POKE КАЖДЫЙ раз при загрузке кода DUMP. Это можно сделать, внеся POKE в процедуру, например:

```text
55000 DEF PROC DUMPHR5
55010 POKE 23074,0 :REM CODES TO
55020 POKE 23075,27:REM ADJUST
55030 POKE 23076,75:REM DUMP FOR
55040 POKE 23067,65:REM AN HR5
55050 POKE 23068,7 :REM PRINTER
55060 DUMP
55070 END PROC
```

Если ты сохранишь этот BASIC, например, командой SAVE "DUMPHR5" (обрати внимание, БЕЗ номера строки для автозапуска), ты сможешь загружать его в любое время или постоянно MERGE'ить в любую программу, где хочешь использовать DUMP. Тебе также нужно будет загрузить код "dmpld", как обычно. Теперь вместо использования DUMP в программе или как прямой команды, используй DUMPHR5, который выполнит POKE, а затем DUMP.

АЛЬТЕРНАТИВНО, конечно, ты можешь добавить в свою программу:

```text
55000 LOAD "dmpld" CODE
55010 POKES....  (ВСЕ POKE)
55020 RUN
```
...затем сохрани программу:
SAVE "NAME" LINE 9000.

Заметь, что если ты используешь второй метод, то DUMP нужно вызывать обычным образом.

В любом случае, я рад, что теперь ты получаешь нормальные дампы на своем принтере.

                        - Brian

От: Gerhard Behr, BRIERFIELD

Вы спрашивали о принтере Citizen 124D. Он у меня уже 6 недель, пришел на замену старому STAR DP 510. У него много интересных особенностей:

1) Заправка бумаги.  
У него толкающий трактор (push tractor feed), и любой, кто привык к тянущему трактору, оценит, сколько бумаги это экономит. Кроме того, он начинает печать на 1/2 дюйма ниже верхнего края. Это можно отрегулировать вручную, что очень удобно для печати адресных этикеток. Если вы хотите использовать отдельные листы, непрерывную рулонную бумагу вынимать не нужно — достаточно нажать клавишу «PARK», чтобы временно убрать её с тракта.

Отдельные листы просто опускаются в направляющую и позиционируются автоматически. Прижимной планки нет, бумага прижимается к валику верхней крышкой. Для обычной работы этого достаточно, но прижим слабоват для печати на некоторых видах конвертов.

2) Шрифты.  
Есть 3 шрифта, переключаемых кнопкой на передней панели: Draft (по качеству не уступает многим NLQ-режимам старых принтеров, скорость 120 симв/сек) и два LQ-шрифта — Times Roman и Courier (скорость 40 симв/сек). Их качество достаточно высокое даже для изготовления слайдов для диапроектора — пожалуй, это самое суровое испытание для любого принтера.

3) Спецэффекты.

### Ответ Brian Cavers для Gerhard Behr

Да, просто загрузите ваш системный диск MGT и выберите пункт «Screen Dump Loader». Либо в любой момент выйдите в BASIC и введите `LOAD "dumpld"CODE`. Теперь код установлен, но помните: его придется загружать заново, если вы сбросите компьютер кнопкой RESET сзади, командой `RANDOMIZE USR 0` или выключите питание. Впрочем, команда `NEW`, по-моему, очищать его не должна.

После установки используйте команду BASIC `DUMP`, чтобы распечатать картинку, или `DUMP CHR$`, чтобы печатать только текст. Если на распечатке появляются странности вроде пропусков в изображении, возможно, потребуется подкорректировать системные переменные.

В таких случаях стоит перечитать мой ответ Julian Bonnebaigt в номере 37, но если возникнут трудности — пишите снова со ВСЕМИ подробностями (т. е. пришлите образец печати или укажите «ничего не напечаталось», опишите любые внесенные изменения, есть ли у вашего принтера специальный графический режим и т. д.).

В вашем случае проблем быть не должно, раз со Спектрума и из FLASH печать идет нормально!

Живой пример использования DUMP можно найти в письме от Philip Seddon через одно после этого.

От: Philip Seddon.

Поскольку в Sam-версиях Outlet нет данных указателя (Index), я решил доработать файл Auto Menu (Outlet 34). На системном диске, шедшем в комплекте с дисководом, есть файл «dumpld». Перенесите этот файл на диск с вашей программой Auto Menu, а затем отредактируйте следующие строки в программе меню:

```text
30 CLEAR 45099:LOAD "dumpld"CODE:(остаток строки не трогать)

430 CLS: CSIZE 8,8: PRINT PAPER 7:PEN 0;(остаток строки не трогать)
```

Отредактируйте конец строки 470, чтобы получилось:
```text
PAPER 7;PEN 0;type$; PAPER 0,520 LET valid$="ZUDLECRPHVSNMTQG" 560 CSIZE 8,8:PRINT #1;PAPER 2; AT 1,0; "          Z=Dump screen"; TAB 30;size$; TAB 0; AT 0,0; menu$(q); TAB 0
```

Перед буквой «Z» в строке 560 идет 10 пробелов. Добавьте следующую новую строку:
```text
215 IF opt$="Z" THEN DUMP
```
Сохраните заново: `SAVE "AUTOMENU" LINE 30`.

Эта модификация прекрасно работает на моем принтере Star LC10. Кроме того, если вы хотите распечатать только одну строку из программы, введите `LLIST N TO N`. Принтер напечатает только строку N, где N — номер нужной строки.

- Philip Seddon
